questions.q: A TV comedy's lead talks to the camera throughout, and nobody else ever notices. In the spirit of Fleabag series 2, what's the strongest way to develop the device?
choices: Drop it after the pilot so it doesn't get stale
Let a character inside the story notice it, so the device becomes plot
Add a second narrator to balance the first
Replace it with voice-over to make it more cinematic
questions.explain: When the Priest notices Fleabag's asides, the device she used to hide becomes the story: someone finally sees her.

questions.q: Fleabag jokes to camera every time a scene gets painful. What is the comedy doing structurally?
choices: Releasing tension so the audience stays relaxed, as in comic relief
Breaking identification so the audience judges the social causes, as Brecht intended
Defending her: the asides are how she avoids the grief she needs to face
Establishing the genre promise of a romantic comedy
questions.explain: The asides are armour. Her want is to stay entertaining and in control; her need is to stop performing and grieve.

questions.q: Why does Fleabag reveal the full story of Boo's death only in the last episode of series 1?
choices: The withheld backstory gives the series a central question and makes the earlier comedy read as avoidance
Television rules require a twist in every finale
The stage version didn't include it
It's an inciting incident, which always comes last in a series
questions.explain: Glimpses keep us asking what happened; the full reveal recasts every joke we laughed at.

questions.q: A playwright is adapting her solo show for television. Which choice best follows what Waller-Bridge did with Fleabag?
choices: Cut the direct address, since TV characters shouldn't know they're watched
Keep every incident exactly as it was on stage
Turn the monologue into a voice-over over silent images
Keep the voice and the spine, and turn described characters into people who can push back
questions.explain: The asides carried the monologue's intimacy to screen, the avoidance stayed the spine, and the sister and father became full characters.

questions.q: At the end of Fleabag series 2, she stops the camera following her. What does this do?
choices: It ends the relationship with the audience: she no longer needs the performance
It's a cliffhanger promising a third series
It shows the Priest has been watching all along
It returns the show to the stage version's ending
questions.explain: The audience was her confidant and her hiding place. Leaving us behind is the last step of the love story.

questions.q: Series 2 opens with Fleabag telling us, 'This is a love story.' What does a line like this mainly do?
choices: It states the theme as a controlling idea for the writers' room
It makes a genre promise to the audience, which the series then twists
It reveals the withheld backstory early
It breaks the three unities
questions.explain: It tells us what kind of story to expect, teasingly, over a disastrous family dinner; the love story turns out to be with a priest.

questions.q: A memoirist keeps telling funny stories around a loss she never names until the end. In Waller-Bridge's terms, what must the late revelation do to earn its place?
choices: Surprise the reader with a twist unrelated to what came before
Arrive in the first paragraph so readers aren't misled
Make the earlier jokes read differently, as avoidance
Be told in the second person
questions.explain: The reveal in Fleabag isn't a twist for its own sake: it explains the comedy we've been laughing at.

ideas: The camera is the character's accomplice: the main relationship is between her and whoever is watching.
Direct address can become plot when someone inside the story notices the asides.
Jokes to the audience can be a character's way of avoiding a grief the story withholds until the end.
A one-woman stage monologue can move to television by keeping its voice and its central avoidance, and giving described people a life of their own.
